title: Direct Murder via Intentional Lethal Poisoning
narrative: A purchased potassium cyanide and surreptitiously mixed it into B's morning drink with the direct intention of causing B's death. B drank the mixture and died within minutes as a direct consequence of the poison. No defensive violence, provocation, or excuse existed.
ground_truth_explanation: Actus reus (CausesDeath) and mens rea (IntentionToCauseDeath) are established under Section 101 Clause (a). No statutory exceptions apply. Murder is fully supported.

title: Murder via Bodily Injury with Subjective Knowledge of Lethality
narrative: A knew that B suffered from a severely diseased and enlarged spleen such that any blunt trauma to B's abdomen was likely to rupture the spleen and cause death. A intentionally struck B in the abdomen with a wooden staff intending to inflict bodily harm. B died of splenic rupture.
ground_truth_explanation: Satisfies Section 101 Clause (b): causing bodily injury with subjective knowledge that the injury is likely to cause death of the particular person harmed.

title: Direct Cheating via Impersonation and Property Delivery
narrative: A falsely represented himself to be an authorized municipal tax collector and intentionally deceived B into believing that B owed overdue property tax fines. Deceived by this falsehood, B handed over ₹50,000 in cash to A, which A pocketed for personal use.
ground_truth_explanation: Satisfies Section 318 Subsection (1): deception combined with fraudulent inducement to deliver property constitutes completed cheating.

title: Exception 1: Grave and Sudden Provocation without Provisos
narrative: Y unexpectedly hurled grave insults, spat in X's face, and violently assaulted X's young child without prior warning. Deprived of self-control by this sudden passion, X picked up a heavy tool and struck Y, causing fatal injuries. The provocation was not sought by X, not done by a public servant, and not done in private defence.
ground_truth_explanation: Prima facie murder under Section 101 Clause (a) is satisfied, but Exception 1 applies fully because grave and sudden provocation occurred without violating any proviso. Liability for murder is defeated and mitigated to Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder.

title: Exception 2: Exceeding Private Defence in Good Faith
narrative: Z ambushed A with an iron club in a dark alley. Believing in good faith that his life was in imminent danger and acting without premeditation, A defended himself with a pocket knife. In the scuffle, A struck Z fatally, exceeding the strict proportion of harm authorized by law, but without intention of doing more harm than he believed necessary for his defense.
ground_truth_explanation: Satisfies Exception 2 of Section 101: good faith exercise of private defence exceeding legal power without premeditation and without intention to do more harm than necessary mitigates murder.

title: Exception 4: Sudden Fight in Heat of Passion
narrative: A sudden verbal dispute erupted between A and B at a crowded marketplace over a minor payment. Both men began fighting in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel without prior premeditation. During the mutual combat, A struck B with a stone, causing fatal head injury. A did not take undue advantage or act in a cruel or unusual manner.
ground_truth_explanation: Satisfies Exception 4 of Section 101: death caused in a sudden fight in heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel without premeditation and without cruelty mitigates murder.

title: Exception 5: Consent of Adult Victim Above Age 18
narrative: B, a competent adult aged 28 suffering from incurable agony, entered into an explicit pact with A begging A to end his life. B took the risk of death with his own informed consent. A administered the fatal dose requested by B.
ground_truth_explanation: Satisfies Exception 5 of Section 101: victim was above age eighteen and suffered death with own consent. Offence is mitigated to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

title: Proviso 1a: Provocation Voluntarily Provoked as an Excuse
narrative: A nurtured a long-standing desire to kill Z. In order to fabricate an excuse, A went to Z's residence and deliberately hurled vulgar insults to provoke Z into striking him. When Z angrily slapped A, A immediately drew a concealed pistol and shot Z dead, claiming sudden provocation.
ground_truth_explanation: Although provocation occurred, Proviso (a) to Exception 1 explicitly bars the defence where provocation was voluntarily sought or provoked by the offender as an excuse. Exception 1 fails; Murder is SUPPORTED.

title: Proviso 1b: Provocation by Public Servant in Lawful Exercise of Power
narrative: Z, a police officer executing a valid arrest warrant issued by a judicial magistrate, lawfully placed A under arrest. A became enraged by the arrest, claimed his dignity was violated, and struck Officer Z with a lethal weapon, killing him.
ground_truth_explanation: Under Proviso (b) to Exception 1, acts done in obedience to law or by a public servant in lawful discharge of duty do not constitute legal provocation. Exception 1 is defeated; Murder is SUPPORTED.

title: Proviso 1c: Provocation in Response to Lawful Private Defence
narrative: A attempted to pull Z's nose and snatch Z's purse. Z, exercising her lawful statutory right of private defence, seized A's wrist to prevent the theft. A became enraged that Z resisted, drew a knife, and stabbed Z to death.
ground_truth_explanation: Under Proviso (c) to Exception 1, provocation given by anything done in lawful exercise of private defence cannot mitigate an offence. Exception 1 fails; Murder is SUPPORTED.

title: Exception 4 Proviso: Offender Taking Undue Advantage in Sudden Fight
narrative: A sudden fistfight broke out between unarmed patrons A and B at a restaurant. In the middle of the scuffle, while B was lying knocked down and disarmed on the floor, A drew a heavy iron wrench and repeatedly struck B on the skull in a cruel and unusual manner, killing B.
ground_truth_explanation: Exception 4 explicitly requires that the offender did NOT take undue advantage or act in a cruel manner. Because A took undue advantage and acted cruelly, Exception 4 is defeated; Murder is SUPPORTED.

title: Missing Mens Rea / Mental State in Death Investigation
narrative: A vehicle operated by A collided with pedestrian B on a roadway, resulting in B's death. The initial FIR documents that A caused B's death. However, investigative findings are completely silent on whether A intended to cause death, intended bodily injury, was reckless, or suffered brake failure.
ground_truth_explanation: Under Open-World Assumption, missing information cannot be presumed false. Culpable mental element (intention or knowledge under Section 101) is missing. Murder cannot be established.

title: Missing Victim Age in Claim of Consent Defence
narrative: A aided Z in jumping into a turbulent canal as part of a mutual pact where Z willingly consented to suffer death. In the criminal proceeding, A claims the benefit of Exception 5. However, no birth certificate or proof of Z's age has been presented, and Z's age remains unknown.
ground_truth_explanation: Exception 5 strictly requires the person consenting to be above eighteen years of age. Because VictimAboveAge18(Z) is unknown, the defence cannot be established.

title: Missing Property Delivery in Cheating Charge
narrative: A exhibited a counterfeit sample of merchandise to prospective buyer B and made false statements. However, the police report contains no record indicating whether B actually delivered any money or whether any transaction took place.
ground_truth_explanation: Section 318 requires deception AND inducement of delivery or harmful act. Because delivery is missing, cheating cannot be verified.

title: Irreconcilable Contradiction in Witness Testimony on Intent
narrative: Prosecution Witness 1 testifies under oath that A aimed and deliberately fired at B with intent to kill. Conversely, the forensic ballistic report and neutral eyewitnesses prove that the weapon suffered an accidental misfire while A was clearing a jam, establishing absence of intention to cause death.
ground_truth_explanation: The premises contain simultaneous assertions of P and ~P regarding IntentionToCauseDeath. The engine flags an evidentiary contradiction requiring judicial resolution.

title: Premeditation Contradicting Sudden Fight Claim
narrative: A claimed he killed B during an unexpected sudden quarrel. However, forensic mobile extractions prove that A had pre-planned the murder 3 days earlier, bought the weapon, and ambushed B in waiting.
ground_truth_explanation: Exception 4 requires absence of premeditation. Because premeditation is proven, the defence is directly contradicted.

title: Cheating Aggravated by Inducing Valuable Security Delivery
narrative: A deceived B regarding a corporate merger and fraudulently induced B to sign and deliver the registered title deeds and share certificates of an estate valued at ₹5 crore.
ground_truth_explanation: Satisfies basic cheating under Section 318 Subsection (1) and triggers aggravated penalty under Subsection (4) for valuable security.

title: Murder Interaction with Mob Lynching Provision
narrative: A mob of six persons (G), including active participant A, acting in concert, cornered and beat B to death solely on the ground of B's religious community.
ground_truth_explanation: Murder is established under Section 101, and Section 103 Subsection (2) explicitly imposes joint capital/life liability on each member of a group of five or more committing murder on discriminatory grounds.

title: Dishonest Concealment Triggering Deception via Explanation
narrative: A sold an estate to B. Knowing that he had no further right in the property, A mortgaged the same property to Z without disclosing the prior sale to B, dishonestly concealing the encumbrance and receiving ₹50 lakh.
ground_truth_explanation: Explanation to Section 318 expands dishonest concealment into Deception. Combined with fraudulent inducement of delivery, Cheating is fully supported.

title: Civil Breach of Contract Disguised as Criminal Cheating
narrative: A contracted with Z to deliver 100 quintals of cotton and took an advance. At the time of receiving the money, A genuinely intended to perform the contract. Later, due to transport strikes and price spikes, A failed to deliver the goods. Z filed a criminal complaint charging A with cheating.
ground_truth_explanation: Under Section 318 Illustration (g), if the offender intends to deliver at the time of agreement and subsequently breaches, it is purely a civil action for breach of contract, NOT criminal cheating.
